profile.headline: Computer Engineer
profile.summary:
I am a Computer Engineer specializing in C++ applications with around 3 years of professional experience.

My background in Computer Engineering allows me to write code while also understanding the hardware it's running on at a deeper level. Instead of throwing my hands up when I run into a bug in the code, I'll pull out the oscilloscope and make sure the code is actually doing what it should be. After all, one can only stare at code for so long before realizing you might have a short on one of the PCB traces mucking up everything.

Some examples of my work include writing driver wrappers for a PCIe device to synchronize timings for a constellation of satellites, building a packet parser to generate telemetry and command packets from an XML file, creating hardware testing scripts, and more. Oh, and some of the code I wrote is currently in space orbiting the earth on a satellite. Totally out of this world!

I grew up in the Midwest, and I graduated Cum Laude from North Dakota State University with a Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering and a minor in Mathematics. Once I graduated, I was ready to explore new opportunities. I packed up my things and moved almost 1000 miles away to Denver, and I haven't looked back since!

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Driver wrapper creation and development for PCIe devices like the Acromag AP482

Ubuntu Based VM deployment script creation for use in a constellation of satellites

HW regression test script creation, development, maintenance, and debug

Full scale integration and testing via Jenkins pipelines

XTCE Parser creation to craft CCSDS Telemetry and Command Packets from XML documents

Embedded Linux programming on devices such as the NXP LS2088A-RDB

Worked in scrum teams varying in size from 5-30 members

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
Research SRAM based in-memory computing

Simulation of SRAM performance in order to calculate delay, area, and power characteristics of certain specifications of SRAM

Utilized programs such as DESTINY, CACTI-M3D, and GEM5 system level architecture simulator to simulate the performance of monolithic inter-tier via stacked dies

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
Worked together closely with a partner as well as a research mentor to investigate how to speed up the processing time of a real Computer Neural Network using Intel's Threading Building Blocks, or TBB, C++ library

Learned the ins and outs of how a neural network works (both the convolutional layer as well as the fully connected network)

Applied the TBB library to our code, and subsequently recorded our testing data and reported our findings

Achieved up to a 7.24x speedup from the original program after application of TBB

honors.title: Dean's List 4x
honors.issuer: Issued by North Dakota State University · Dec 2021
